name: Maurice Gilbert
bio: Member of Wilde's Paris circle of the exile years, on first-name terms ('Maurice') with the whole inner circle. During Wilde's final illness in November 1900 he came to the sickroom almost daily alongside Reggie Turner, though Turner noted he 'does not like being in the room'; at Robert Ross's request he took the (unsuccessful) photograph of Wilde on his deathbed. He was one of the nine named mourners who walked behind the hearse to St Germain des Prés and is listed among the senders of funeral wreaths. The editors' main particulars are sparse: except that his father was English and his mother French, and that he was a young soldier in the marine infantry, nothing is known of him.
bio_sources: Nicholas Frankel, Oscar Wilde: The Unrepentant Years (2017), p. 209 - 'about whom very little is known'
bio_note: All facts from the Epilogue of Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000): sickroom attendance from Turner's letters to Ross, pp. 1217-19 (repo PDF 1262-64); photograph, procession roll-call and wreath list from Ross to Adey, 14 Dec. 1900, p. 1222 (PDF 1267). Pages read as page images 2026-08-03; printed folios confirmed. Full passages in dossiers/ADEY-GILBERT-TURNER_dossier.md. Birth/death dates not sourced in the pages read. The dossier's 'shared intimate' hypothesis (Wilde/Ross/Douglas) rests on secondary literature not yet read in the source; the planned reads of the letter at printed p. 1084 and the General Index mention pages were not completed (predecessor session cut off) - no romantic or sexual claim about Gilbert appears in any passage transcribed so far. Main-particulars footnote at Complete Letters (2000), p. 1025 n. 4, transcribed by the correspondents pass 2026-08-03. Birth and death dates are not recorded in the edition. DATES: NOT FOUND, AND TWO SOURCES STATE POSITIVELY THAT THE RECORD DOES NOT CARRY THEM (2026-08-03). The Complete Letters editors, at the main-particulars footnote already cited above (printed p. 1025 n. 4), write that 'Except that his father was English and his mother French, and that he was a young soldier in the marine infantry, nothing is known of him.' Nicholas Frankel, Oscar Wilde: The Unrepentant Years (Harvard, 2017), printed p. 209 (repo PDF 223, read as a rendered page image so far and the folio confirmed), calls him 'a young man named Maurice Gilbert, a one-time marine infantryman, the son of a French mother and an English father - Wilde called him "all French lily and English rose" - about whom very little is known except what can be gleaned from Wilde's surviving letters'. Also searched without result: every 'Maurice Gilbert' occurrence in the Complete Letters OCR mirror (PDF 602, 1071, 1100, 1119, 1130, 1221, 1252, 1267) and Frankel's index. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted. Note the small discrepancy between the two: the Letters say his father was English and his mother French, Frankel writes 'a French mother and an English father' - the same parentage, stated in the same order, no conflict.
